members.duties: mechanics audit: damage-budget compliance (flat numbers on Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21), prereq shapes (Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3), cost math (cards 2/4/8), level gates, dice remnants, stale vocabulary, cross-chapter contradictions
consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance
final quality: structure, cross-references, missing content, completeness

payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 9, Talents & Abilities (quarto-book/chapters/09-talents-abilities.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the Heroes of Legend
TTRPG rulebook and produce a disposition plan. Do NOT fix anything; file findings only.

## Scope
The registered source `09-talents` (the chapter's .qmd). This chapter is the source of record for
three card families: 21 Talents, 4 Basic Attacks, and 17 Weapon Maneuvers (42 cards, no tables).
Other chapters depend on it and mirror it: ch15 (equipment, "weapons follow the cards"), ch05
(class ability tables), ch13 (combat, conditions, the crit/fumble tables), ch16 (armor and shields),
ch22 (reference sheets), ch19 (GM guidance). Cross-check against the authoritative chapters only
where a claim is canon-determined: attributes ch03, disciplines/ladder/budget ch08, advancement
and the DP economy ch18, core resolution/tiers/difficulty/Boon-Bane ch06, combat and the condition
table ch13, social ch14, armor ch16, equipment ch15, spells ch11 and ch12, class abilities ch05,
glossary ch21.

## Locked conventions the chapter must satisfy (cite the violated convention in every finding)
- **Damage budget is FLAT.** Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21 on Weak/Standard/Strong.
  No damage dice anywhere; the only sanctioned dice are 3d6 one-roll checks, 4d6 for Boon/Bane
  (keep highest or lowest three), and explicit random-effect tables (d6 criticals and fumbles).
- **One-roll principle:** the attack or casting roll IS the damage roll. Zero separate damage rolls.
- **Two printed damage expressions, and their bases are fixed.** FLAT uses the row as listed.
  ATTRIBUTE-SCALED adds the card's stated attribute to a base value: Novice cards use the
  Basic-card floor 1/2/3 (ch08:248, ch09's own basic attacks, ch15:60), Adept and Master cards use
  the row minus 3 (3/6/9 and 6/12/18). Melee adds Brawn (Finesse may substitute Agility); missile
  and thrown attacks are FLAT with no attribute added. Minimum 1 damage.
- **Card costs are flat 2/4/8 DP at Novice/Adept/Master for every class.** Gates: Adept at Level 3,
  Master at Level 7.
- **Prerequisite shapes:** a card's tier equals the number of Disciple ranks it requires. Novice = 1
  rank, Adept = EXACTLY 2 ranks, Master = EXACTLY 3 ranks (3 different, 2+1, or 3 same). Maximum 3
  ranks in any one Discipline. Weapon cards gate on the weapon Disciplines (Blades, Axes, Polearms,
  Archery, Heavy Weapon, Unarmed).
- **ZERO flat +N damage riders (book-wide law, weapons rework 2026-08-19).** No card anywhere may add
  a flat damage number. The ONLY sanctioned damage booster is the tier bump, always phrased "+1
  damage tier" (use the row one step above on the budget), the Overchannel convention. A card whose
  base hit also deals damage cannot then stack a recurring damage rider on an off-table sum: base hit
  plus rider must land on a budget row or the rider must gate on the WEAK result (for example a
  Novice Weak 2 plus a 2 rider = 4 is on the row; gating the same rider on Strong is not).
- **ZERO numeric roll modifiers (Boon/Bane law).** A situational bonus or penalty to a ROLL is Boon
  or Bane, never +N or −N. Numbers are reserved for damage, HP, DR, DP, ranges and durations, plus
  three named exceptions: attributes and skill tiers (Novice +1, Adept +2, Master +3), the DA's
  difficulty dial, and a Challenge penalty. Boons and Banes cancel one for one, and the potence
  ladder is Boon/Bane 1 = 4d6 keep three, 2 = 5d6, 3 = 6d6, capped at three.
- **Leveled condition vocabulary.** Conditions use the leveled form (Burning 3, Slowed 5, Dazed 1,
  Asleep 2, Frozen X) as ch13's condition table defines them, or the binary name exactly (Prone,
  Frightened, Restrained, Blinded, Dazed, Hidden). Bespoke paraphrases ("take 2 ongoing fire
  damage", "slowed for 1 round" with no level, "Frozen in place") are defects.
- **Card Template v2.** A card is `Name (type)`, then a header line carrying Disciplines per tier,
  Action, Range or Area, Duration and Keywords, then body paragraphs. PASSIVE cards (talents,
  Action: Passive) are the exception: they list Novice/Adept/Master only, where Novice carries the
  full effect (Strong) and Adept and Master are strict supersets. Every card states its damage
  expression (Flat or Attribute-Scaled) in its damage line.
- **Zero em-dashes in book text (style law, book-wide).**
- **Cross-references:** every @sec-* / @tbl-* link must resolve to a real label, and no typed period
  may follow a cross-reference (the engine renders its own, so `@sec-x.` prints a doubled stop).
- **Typst conventions (MIGRATION-SPEC):** exactly one `{=typst}` fence per file with the `# H1` line
  kept above it; callout bodies in the NAMED `body: [...]` form (the positional form is silently
  dropped by the theme); every `#table(` carries `outlined: false`; `#label("sec-...")` on the line
  after its heading.
- **Phantom cards.** Any card named in this chapter must exist under exactly that name wherever else
  it is referenced, and any card this chapter references must exist somewhere in the book. A name
  that collides with a different card's name in another chapter is a defect.

## Findings format (one finding per member this round)
Each finding must be decision-oriented: name the broken value with [09-talents-abilities:LINE], the
expected or correct value, the violated convention, and the minimal fix. Cite cross-chapter canon
lines where the expected value is canon-determined. Recompute every number you check; a card's
damage line, its tier, its Discipline count and its cost must all agree with each other and with the
chapters that mirror them. A finding that cannot state the broken value and the expected value is
not a finding. Do NOT invent defects to look thorough; a chapter with few real problems is a good
outcome.

payload.argument: Disposition: not publishable as-is, though every fault I found is a one-line fix. I verified the card families by grepping the chapter's level-three headings: twenty talent cards, four basic attack cards and seventeen weapon maneuver cards, forty-two in all, with no tables, matching the scope the brief sets. I then recomputed every printed damage band against the fixed budget. The melee basic and the two missile basics sit on the basic-card floor, the unarmed card uses the weaker floor that the equipment chapter confirms for bare hands, and the damaging maneuvers land on the novice, adept and master rows, with the single exception below. Tier counts check out for all seventeen maneuvers against the discipline chapter's rule that a card's tier equals its prerequisite count, including the shield card, whose two-Armor gate the discipline chapter itself prints as an adept entry. Costs, the three cross-reference labels, the lone typst fence and the zero-em-dash rule all pass, and the figure caption's number matches the book's global figure offset, so it is not a defect. Three clusters do fail. First, a passive reaction talent's adept rank grants a flat initiative bonus, a numeric roll modifier the Boon and Bane law forbids outside its named exceptions; the minimal fix is to make it a Boon instead. Second, two passive talents shed a benefit at master rank rather than strictly containing the adept rank, so the template's superset rule is broken; the minimal fix is to carry the lower effect forward. Third, a shield maneuver prints the basic-attack floor across its novice band where the novice flat row belongs; the minimal fix is to raise that band one step. Each is a one-line change, but the chapter as printed should not ship.

evidence.claim: A passive reaction talent's adept rank hands out a flat initiative bonus, which is a numeric roll modifier the Boon and Bane law does not license outside its named exceptions.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Adept:* You gain one extra Reaction per round and +1 Initiative.

evidence.claim: That talent's master rank grants an extra reaction but drops the initiative bonus the adept rank carried, so the top rank does not strictly contain the rank below it.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Master:* You gain two extra Reactions per round.

evidence.claim: The glossary defines a talent as an always-on passive benefit that needs no activation, yet seven of the chapter's talents carry an active Action, four of them Reactions.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Talent:* A passive benefit purchased with DP. Always on.

evidence.claim: The critical-hit talent's adept rank adds a splash hit against one adjacent enemy.
That talent's master rank prints only a capped strong-damage value, so it drops the adjacent-target splash and fails the superset requirement for passive cards.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Master:* On a Critical, the attack deals maximum Strong damage (21).

evidence.claim: The shield maneuver's novice band prints a one, two, three flat progression, which is the basic-attack floor rather than the novice flat row.
Canon's budget table fixes the novice flat row at two, four and six, and canon directs flat damage to take the row exactly as printed.

payload.argument: Tested the leading support position that the 42 cards all land inside the flat damage budget; it breaks on stacking. The chapter itself rules that bonuses from different talents combine, and several effects each move a hit up one or more outcome tiers with no shared ceiling. Weapon Focus at Master adds three tiers to any ability card in its chosen weapon Discipline, Dangerous Gambit adds a fourth on a 12-or-higher roll twice per scene, and Power Strike or Charge each add one more. A Master-tier Strong result is already 21 and is the top row of the budget table, so even the two-talent core (Weapon Focus plus Dangerous Gambit, four tiers) has no row above it to land on, and adding a maneuver reaches roughly six tiers past the table. Broken value: stacked +N-tier riders push a hit off the printed budget. Expected: every result lands on a real row, or one global ceiling governs all tier bumps. The chapter shows it knows a cap is needed because Death Blow alone prints maximum 21, but that cap is applied to one card in 42. Same missing-limit gap has two more counter-examples: Combat Reflexes Master grants two extra Reactions yet silently drops the Adept tier's +1 Initiative, so Master is not a strict superset, and Riposte is a Reaction counterattack with no per-scene or per-round limit, so the extra Reactions convert directly into repeated full-damage counterattacks in a single round. Minimal fix: one rule that no result may rise above Strong for its card's rank, absolute maximum 21, applied to every tier-boost effect, plus usage lines on Reaction maneuvers.

evidence.claim: The chapter explicitly sanctions combining separate talents' bonuses, which is the stacking hook the overflow rides on.
Weapon Focus at Master adds three damage tiers to ability cards of one chosen weapon Discipline, uncapped and repeatable each attack.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +3 damage tiers on ability cards of the chosen weapon Discipline

evidence.claim: Dangerous Gambit raises the outcome one tier on a 14-plus roll, and its Master line does so twice per scene; this stacks with Weapon Focus.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: increase the damage tier of the result by one

evidence.claim: Power Strike is a weapon maneuver that moves the next weapon attack up one tier with no per-scene restriction, so it can feed the same boosted attack as the talents.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +1 damage tier on your next weapon attack

evidence.claim: Charge is a second tier bump a character can aim at the same pending attack on a later turn.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: make one attack at +1 damage tier

evidence.claim: Only Death Blow carries a ceiling; the omission of the same cap on every other tier booster is the defect.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: (one row up on the damage budget, maximum 21)

evidence.claim: Combat Reflexes Master grants two extra Reactions but silently drops the Adept tier's Initiative bonus, so the Master line is not a strict superset of Adept as passive cards require.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You gain two extra Reactions per round

evidence.claim: The Adept line is the tier being superseded and it includes an Initiative bonus the Master line omits.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one extra Reaction per round and +1 Initiative

evidence.claim: Riposte's Master tier counterattacks for the full Master row and prints no usage limit, so extra Reactions translate into repeated counterattacks within one round.
Renewal is the only weapon maneuver that prints an explicit usage cap, confirming the family has no consistent default limit.

payload.argument: I parsed the chapter programmatically instead of reading it impressionistically. What verifies clean: exactly 42 cards, split 21 Talents / 4 Basic Attacks / 17 Weapon Maneuvers, matching the scope claim; every one of the 17 maneuver Discipline counts sits on the locked ladder (1, 2 or 3 ranks, no outlier of 4+); all three @sec-* tokens resolve against real labels; exactly one typst fence; no typed stop after a cross-reference; and the sweeps return zero em-dashes, zero en-dashes and zero damage dice, so the flat-budget spine and the no-dice law hold on this file. The damage rows are where it breaks. Of the seventeen maneuvers, seven print a numeric Weak/Standard/Strong row, and five of those seven print a row below the tier their own Discipline count selects: Riposte at 2 Blades (Adept) prints 2/4/6 where 6/9/12 is owed; Shield Slam at 2 Armor prints 1/2/3; Parry at 2 Blades prints a 2/4/6 DR row; Brace at 2 Polearms prints 2/4/6; Cyclone at 3 Blades (Master) prints 2/4/6 where 9/15/21 is owed. Dual Strike and Renewal, both 1 rank, are the only on-row cases. Violated convention: the tier-keyed flat damage budget plus the rule that a card's tier is set by its Discipline rank count. ch08:229-230 fixes those rows and ch08:120-122 canonises Shield Slam as the two-rank Adept example, so the expected values are canon-determined rather than preference, and an Adept sibling card in ch12 prints the Adept row as its base. Two knock-on effects: each broken base is followed on the same card by Adept 6/9/12 and Master 9/15/21 rows, so a two-rank buyer reaches the top row for Adept DP, and a three-rank buyer does so for less. The numeric-roll sweep leaves exactly one survivor, the +1 Initiative on Combat Reflexes at line 41, which the book-wide Boon/Bane law converted everywhere else including this chapter's own sibling talents. The flat-rider sweep found no off-row riders; the only standalone flat damage number on a card, Death Blow's 6 to an adjacent enemy, lands on the Novice Strong row.

evidence.claim: Riposte carries 2 Blades, an Adept gate, but its three base outcomes print the Novice 2/4/6 row instead of the Adept 6/9/12 row the budget owes; its own Adept line already prints 6/9/12.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: When an enemy deals Weak damage to you, counterattack for 2

evidence.claim: Cyclone carries 3 Blades, a Master gate, yet its three base outcomes print the Novice 2/4/6 row, with 9/15/21 owed; it is the only three-rank card in the file.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Hit all adjacent enemies for 2 damage

evidence.claim: Shield Slam carries 2 Armor, an Adept gate, but prints 1/2/3, which is the attribute-scaled Novice floor rather than a flat row, on a card that adds no attribute to its damage.
Brace carries 2 Polearms, an Adept gate, but prints 2/4/6 for the damage its target takes; Parry (2 Blades, also Adept) prints the same 2/4/6 shape as its DR row.
The authoritative budget table keys the printed row to the tier, so 2 Disciplines pays 6/9/12 and 3 Disciplines pays 9/15/21.
The ladder rule makes the rank count the card's tier, and the same table lists Shield Slam as the two-rank Adept example, fixing its expected row at 6/9/12.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A card requiring 2 Fire is Adept.

evidence.claim: A two-rank sibling card in another chapter prints the Adept row 6/9/12 as its base outcomes, the pattern ch09's maneuver cards depart from.
The numeric-roll sweep leaves one survivor: Combat Reflexes grants an extra Reaction alongside a flat +1 Initiative, a numeric bonus to the initiative roll rather than a Boon.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one extra Reaction per round and +1 Initiative

evidence.claim: Recount: 42 cards parse as 21/4/17; the 17 maneuver ranks are all 1, 2 or 3; 7 maneuvers print a numeric row; 5 of those 7 are one or two tiers low; the 4 basic attacks use the 1/1/2 and 1/2/3 floors.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 5 of 7 numeric rows fall a tier below their gate

payload.argument: One Weapon Maneuver breaks the flat damage budget. Shield Slam cites a 2 Armor prerequisite (Adept, 2 ranks) and its Weak/Standard/Strong lines print 1/2/3 at lines 377-381, but the card is a flat-damage maneuver, not a Basic Attack, so its base row must be the Novice row 2/4/6, with 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 already following at lines 383 and 385. The 1/2/3 value is the attribute-scaled Basic-card floor and only applies where a stated attribute is added; Shield Slam adds none, so 1/2/3 is off-budget. Broken value 1/2/3, expected 2/4/6. Every sibling flat maneuver confirms the row: Riposte, Cyclone, Brace and Renewal each open at 2/4/6, and Dual Strike totals 2/4/6, so Shield Slam is the lone outlier. Minimal fix: raise lines 377/379/381 to 2/4/6 damage. Separately, Weapon Focus escalates the booster to +2 and +3 damage tiers at lines 61 and 63; the convention sanctions only the single-step tier bump expressed as +1 damage tier, and a three-step bump on a Master row (21) leaves the budget table, so those two lines exceed the allowed booster and should be restated as single-step bumps. Cost, gate and Discipline-count math are otherwise sound: costs sit at 2/4/8 with the Level 3 and Level 7 gates, and no card requires more than 3 ranks, so the max-3 ladder holds.

evidence.claim: Shield Slam prints 1/2/3 as flat maneuver damage; as a 2-Armor flat card it should sit on the Novice row 2/4/6, so all three lines are one step low.
Riposte, the neighboring 2-rank Blades maneuver, keys its base damage to 2/4/6 then 6/9/12 and 9/15/21, showing the row Shield Slam should match.
Cyclone also opens at 2/4/6 for a 3-rank card, confirming the Novice base row is the norm for flat maneuvers.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Hit all adjacent enemies for 2 damage

evidence.claim: Weapon Focus scales to two and then three damage tiers, exceeding the single sanctioned tier bump; the Adept and Master lines need single-step phrasing.
Recomputed every flat row in the chapter: 2/4/6, 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 all hold except Shield Slam's base 1/2/3, and no card exceeds 3 required ranks.

payload.argument: The Talent family is described twice as passive and permanently live [09-talents-abilities:13], [21-glossary:85], yet seven of the twenty-one talent cards are activated, limited-use cards: Fortune's Favor spends a Reaction [09-talents-abilities:27], Refuse to Fall a Reaction [:97], Miracle Worker a Reaction [:127], Battlefield Assessment a full Action [:177], Quick Study a Free action [:187], Chaotic Insight a Reaction [:197], and Rally the Troops a Maneuver [:207]. The glossary even names Fortune's Favor as its illustration of a talent while declaring the category activation-free, so the same word names two kinds of card. Term consistency also slips on usage limits: Renewal folds its per-scene limit into the Action field at [09-talents-abilities:529] where every other limited card states the limit in the body, and the same frequency phrase wanders between the front and back of a line within one card (Miracle Worker Novice [:129] versus Adept [:131]). Minimal fix: widen both definitions to say talents may be passive or limited-use activated cards, correct the glossary's example, and standardize the usage-limit phrase and its position in card bodies.

evidence.claim: The chapter opening splits cards in two and says talents are never switched on, leaving activation to abilities.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Talents are passive. They change your numbers

evidence.claim: Fortune's Favor occupies a Reaction, so this talent must be spent and cannot be permanently live as defined.
Battlefield Assessment is a second talent whose action slot calls for a full Action rather than standing passive.
The glossary entry defines a talent as passive and needing no activation, then offers an activated card as its example of one.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A passive benefit purchased with DP. Always on.

evidence.claim: Renewal alone hides its per-scene limit inside the Action header instead of stating it in the body as the other cards do.
Miracle Worker's Adept row leads with the frequency while its own Novice row trails with it, so limit placement drifts inside a single card.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Once per scene, when an ally within 30 ft drops

payload.argument: The chapter is not yet publishable because its card-type definition contradicts its own cards and the glossary. It states that talents are always on and never activated [09-talents-abilities:13][09-talents-abilities:15], yet seven cards typed Talent carry an activation Action: Fortune's Favor is a Reaction [09-talents-abilities:27], Quick Study is Free [09-talents-abilities:187], Rally the Troops is a Maneuver [09-talents-abilities:207]. The glossary repeats the always-on claim and explicitly names Fortune's Favor as an example [21-glossary:85], so the same card is passive in canon and Reaction in this chapter. Separately, no header line in the file carries a Duration field, nor a duration folded into Range, although the chapter's own card template requires one and the spell chapters carry it; every header stops at Disciplines, Action, Range and Keywords [09-talents-abilities:243]. Fourth, the statement that each maneuver is gated by a weapon Discipline [09-talents-abilities:301] is false for Shield Slam, gated on 2 Armor [09-talents-abilities:375] (canon-confirmed [08-disciplines:122]) and Renewal, gated on 1 Protection [09-talents-abilities:529]. Minimal fix: reword the Talent definition so triggered talents are permitted (and align the glossary), add the missing Duration header field to all 42 cards, and correct the gating sentence at [09-talents-abilities:301]. Cross-reference integrity itself is clean: every @sec-* link resolves and no typed period follows one.

evidence.claim: The chapter defines talents as passive and always on, implying no activation step.
Fortune's Favor is typed Talent but its header gives an activation Action, contradicting the passive definition.
The glossary calls talents activation-free and names Fortune's Favor, the same card this chapter types as a Reaction.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Does not require activation. Examples: Tough

evidence.claim: A representative card header lists only four fields, none of them Duration, and this pattern repeats on all 42 cards.
The chapter asserts every weapon maneuver is gated by a weapon Discipline.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Each is gated by weapon Disciplines.

evidence.claim: Shield Slam is typed Weapon Maneuver but gated on 2 Armor, not a weapon Discipline; canon confirms the Armor gate.
The disciplines chapter's prerequisite table lists Shield Slam against 2 Armor, so line 301's blanket weapon-Discipline claim cannot stand.

payload.argument: The card typography itself is clean. Forty-two level-3 card headings sit consistently under three level-2 family sections, each of the three families opens on a fresh page behind a page break, every one of the forty-two one-line stat blocks prints complete with its Keywords field present, and no em-dash character occurs in the chapter's own prose. The failure is page flow. Each card is a bare heading followed by loose paragraphs, with nothing binding the pieces into one unit, so five of the forty-two cards are cut by a page turn and one card's name is left stranded alone at the foot of a page. The book's own theme already treats this as a defect class, wrapping tables so a rule block cannot tear and documenting a fix for a heading left alone at a page foot, yet the card chapter has no comparable wrapper. The table cost is real: a GM mid-encounter has to flip the page to finish reading a card's Weak/Standard/Strong rows. Minimal fix: render each card inside a single non-breaking block (a show rule on level-three headings that binds the heading to the content that follows it, or a card div set to unbreakable), which is safe here because every card is far shorter than one text block; verify on a clean build that no card splits and no heading strands.

evidence.claim: The Arcane Reservoir card name prints alone as the last line of p145, and its stat line plus body paragraphs open p146, so the heading is orphaned from its own card.
Basic Unarmed is torn mid-card: the heading, stat line and Weak row sit on p149, and the remaining four rows continue at the top of p150.
Cleave prints its Weak and Standard rows at the foot of p151 and resumes with the Strong, Adept and Master rows on p152.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Weak: Hit one target. If it drops to 0 HP

evidence.claim: Disarm splits the same way: heading, stat line and Weak row on p152, with the Standard, Strong, Adept and Master rows on p153.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Weak: The target keeps its grip.

evidence.claim: The theme already wraps tables in a non-breaking block and records a fix for headings left alone at a page foot, so the card chapter's absence of any keep-together wrapper is inconsistent with the book's own standard.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: unbreakable blocks so they stay intact on one page

evidence.claim: All forty-two stat lines render whole on one line each with the Keywords field intact, so no card loses a field or wraps its Discipline/Action/Range line.
Three level-2 family sections each follow a page break, with forty-two level-3 card headings and no level-4 heading anywhere, so the heading ladder has no skipped levels.

dissent.position: Refuted and stands; counter-signal on the cleared spine: verified the 42-card set (21/4/17, no tables), all 17 maneuver rank counts on the ladder, the 2/4/8 costs and Level 3/7 gates, three resolving @sec labels, one typst fence, zero em-dashes and the figure-number offset. Its three defect clusters (Initiative Boon, the two superset breaks, Shield Slam off-row) all hold; its Shield Slam expected value 2/4/6 is adopted one step further at the canon-fixed 6/9/12.

Refuted and stands; its stress test of the budget is what surfaced the missing global tier-boost ceiling (Weapon Focus plus Dangerous Gambit plus a maneuver exits the table while only Death Blow caps at 21), and it corroborated the Combat Reflexes superset break. Its Reaction-limit and Riposte points are recorded as a veto-able design default, not as a hard defect. Adopted.

Refuted and stands; its programmatic read is the finding the disposition rests on: five of the seven numeric-row maneuvers print a base below their own rank's tier, and the numeric-roll sweep leaves exactly one survivor (Combat Reflexes' Initiative). Its card count, rank ladder, reference resolution, fence count, dash sweep and dice sweep are all confirmed. Adopted.

Refuted and stands on Weapon Focus: '+2/+3 damage tiers' exceed the single sanctioned '+1 damage tier' booster. Its Shield Slam finding is adopted but its expected value is corrected: the canon-fixed base is 6/9/12 (Shield Slam is the two-rank Adept example at 08-disciplines:122), not the Novice row 2/4/6; on the other four off-tier maneuvers it read the printed Novice base as intentional, which the tier-keyed budget does not support.

Refuted and stands; its two findings (the passive-versus-activated Talent contradiction with the glossary, and the usage-limit placement drift at Renewal 09:529 and Miracle Worker 09:129) were both implemented in a8b496d. Its voice findings are accepted; no part of this finding is rebutted.

Refuted and stands on two of three: the passive-versus-activated contradiction (with the glossary) and the false 'gated by weapon Disciplines' sentence at 09:301 are implemented in a8b496d. Its third claim, that every card lacks a Duration header field, is dismissed: no chapter prints a Duration field and the spell chapters fold duration into Range, so 09:15 accurately describes its own headers.

Refuted and stands as the only render-lens finding: five of forty-two cards were split by a page turn and one heading was stranded at a page foot, with no keep-together wrapper on the card band. Recorded as an open layout item to re-verify on a clean build because the theme changed twice after the sampled PDF (#84/#476 orphaned-heading fix, #478 continuous folios); not re-litigated.

payload.rationale: Seven members filed on topic t-01; all seven refuted, none supported, and no finding carries a rebuttal, so seven refutes stand against the charter's quorum of 4 and the topic closes on a terminal reject-majority. No judge was needed and no ruling was sealed, so rulings_applied is empty by construction. The refutes converge on three clusters rather than on a single defect. (1) The Talent category contradicts itself: f-005 (author) and f-006 (editor-in-chief) independently found that the chapter and 21-glossary:85 call talents activation-free while seven Talent cards carry an activation, and f-001 (librarian) carried the same mismatch in evidence. (2) Two passive cards break the template's superset rule: f-001 and f-002 agree on Combat Reflexes (Master drops the Adept initiative bonus) and f-001 alone caught Death Blow (Master drops the adept adjacent-target splash). (3) Combat Reflexes' '+1 Initiative' is the last numeric roll modifier standing after the Boon/Bane wave, flagged independently by f-001 and f-003. f-006 adds the false gating sentence at 09:301, canon-confirmed by 08-disciplines:122, and f-005 adds the usage-limit placement drift. All five of those clusters were implemented in the council-pass commit a8b496d (PR #482) and verified on current main. Two member positions required adjudication. FIRST, the maneuver base rows. f-003 (researcher) filed five numeric-row maneuvers as one or two tiers low; f-001 and f-004 read the same lines and concluded that flat maneuvers simply open on the Novice row, so only Shield Slam (printing the non-row 1/2/3) was a defect, expected 2/4/6. The tier-keyed reading is adopted. The reasons: 08-disciplines:133 and :208 make a card's tier equal its prerequisite count (Shield Slam's 2 Armor makes it Adept); 08-disciplines:228-230 key the damage row to that tier; 08-disciplines:240 gives the worked statement 'An Adept Brimstone Burst deals 6/9/12', and Brimstone Burst is itself a two-rank card whose printed base is 6/9/12; 08-disciplines:246 says Flat takes the row exactly as listed; and 08-disciplines:122 canonises Shield Slam as the two-rank Adept example, which fixes its expected base at 6/9/12, not 2/4/6. The ch12 siblings corroborate (2 Religion/2 Life cards print the Adept row as their base), and the ch08 council's own Pillar of Light ruling (decisions-pending #23) fixed a two-rank card that printed the wrong row to the Adept row and fixed Hallowed Ground's DR row to 6/9/12, which is exactly Parry's shape. So f-003's five-card count stands and f-001/f-004 were under-corrected on Shield Slam; the correction does not change any card's live damage value because each card's Adept line already prints the right row. SECOND, f-006's Duration claim is dismissed after checking the whole book: no chapter prints a Duration header field, and the spell chapters fold duration into the Range parenthetical, so 09:15 describes its own headers accurately; this is a template-spec question routed out, not a ch09 defect. f-002's stacking finding survives as open: the chapter permits talent bonuses to combine and ships multiple uncapped tier boosters while only Death Blow states 'maximum 21', and 15-equipment:220 shows the local ceiling already exists elsewhere in the book, so the fix is one global ceiling rule. f-004's Weapon Focus finding also survives: the only sanctioned booster phrasing is '+1 damage tier', so '+2/+3 damage tiers' are outside it. f-007's page-flow finding is layout and is recorded for re-verification because the theme changed after the sampled PDF. One cross-chapter nit was routed out (07-skills:132 points at combat for a maneuver that lives here). Net: the numeric and taxonomic spine is clean, the cleared ground is large (42-card set, ranks, costs, gates, labels, fences, dashes, dice, basic floors), and the reject rests on a short, fully-enumerated list.
